newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama's casinos eyed by 34 foreign firms.
newsitem.headline: Panama's casinos eyed by 34 foreign firms.

text.p: Thirty-four international firms are eyeing operating Panama's 20 casinos, a top government official said Friday.

Panama closed the pre-qualification process Thursday and plans to announce the qualifying companies on November 15, Alfredo Macia, head of the government's privatization program, told Reuters. A public bid is scheduled for early February.

The government intends to contract three companies, one to operate slot machines and two to operate the casinos which are located in hotels throughout Panama City and the Atlantic port city of Colon, 50 miles (80 km) from Panama City.
Annual casino revenues hover around $7 million and the government hopes to double or triple that amount when foreign companies take over operations, Macia said.
Panama's Constitution prohibits the sale of the casinos but foreign companies can operate them.
